mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate investments and consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) decline by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals a weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate revenues and earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals a strong supply-side expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate revenues and economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate is above 4.5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) shows a year-over-year increase of less than 2%, it signals a disinflationary environment under tight monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate a potential pivot to easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint condition of high FEDFUNDS and low CPIAUCSL inflation does not correlate with positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.5% in the same period, it signals a significant weakening in both housing demand and labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate a broader economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and UNRATE increases > 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint condition of declining HOUST and rising UNRATE does not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2%) suggests accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate higher liquidity and lower borrowing costs.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2%, or if the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
